description: Hi, I’m Bishrel the team leader and we are Team Florensiza. We're interested in Earth science, climate data and design. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 we're taking on an incredible challenge and we wish goodluck to every participants!
summary: Is Mongolia's climate really changing? Most people guess. Earth System Trend Detective lets anyone check. It is a free web tool that turns 45 years of NASA data (the MERRA-2 model and CERES satellites, through NASA POWER) into answers to the challenge's four questions: what is changing, where, by how much, and is it significant? Pick one of 14 variables and a place, from a single point on Earth to the whole of Mongolia, and the app charts the trend, runs two significance tests (a t-test with a 95% confidence interval, and the Mann-Kendall test) and explains the verdict in plain words. A scanner finds which variables are moving, a clickable map shows where, and guided missions make students guess before they see the evidence. What makes it matter is honesty: it doesn't just draw a trend line, it tells you whether to believe it. Mongolia, for example, has warmed 0.18 °C per decade since 1981, significantly across more than half the country, but its summers are warming while its winters are not.
details: In Mongolia, every grandparent has a climate story: the winter that took the herd, the summer the river barely ran. Stories matter, but they can't tell a real trend from one bad year. NASA has measured and modeled Earth's climate for decades. The hard part is knowing which graphs to look at, and whether a change is real or just noise. My project, Earth System Trend Detective turns that data into evidence anyone can check.
